engagement_summary: 4 items flagged across: anti-dilution, cap table, dual class.

items.title: Stale current_conversion_price detected
items.applies_when: Use when the cap table records an earlier anti-dilution adjustment for a series whose conversion price still equals its original — the two cannot both be right.
items.founder_question: Cap-state inconsistency detected: current_conversion_price equals original_conversion_price on a preferred series, but cap_table_history shows a prior anti_dilution_applied event for that series. Indicates someone reset CCP after AD without persisting the change, or attached history without persisting CCP. Counsel reviews to verify which value is authoritative.
items.counsel_question: Cap-state inconsistency detected: current_conversion_price equals original_conversion_price on a preferred series, but cap_table_history shows a prior anti_dilution_applied event for that series. items.title: Preferred pricing unknown — anti-dilution and 1:1 conversion assumption disclosed to counsel
items.applies_when: Use when the price of at least one preferred series is unknown. Does not fire when every series has a known price.
items.founder_question: One or more preferred series is marked the unknown-pricing flag because the founder/mapper could not confirm the actual original_issue_price / original_conversion_price / current_conversion_price. The skill substitutes a numeric $1.00 sentinel for all three prices (so the schema's required-numeric and >0 gates pass without fabricating a real price) and forces anti_dilution_protection to 'none' for that series, since anti-dilution adjustment formulas are defined against the original issue/conversion price and cannot be run against a placeholder. This means anti-dilution and liquidation preference are NOT modeled for the series, and the conversion ratio is assumed 1:1 (original_conversion_price == current_conversion_price == 1.0) — i.e. no historical down-round adjustment is reflected even if one in fact occurred. Counsel/founder must confirm the actual issuance terms before relying on ownership, dilution, or preference figures involving this series.

items.title: Dual-class voting structure detected — investor objections likely at later rounds
items.applies_when: Use when any founder or common holder carries a voting multiple above one vote per share.
items.founder_question: A founder or common-batch holder carries a voting_rights_multiple greater than 1.0 (super-voting common; typically class_b with 10x voting). Series A and later investors frequently push back on dual-class structures during diligence; NVCA model docs and Carta benchmarks both note that ratification of dual-class can require negotiation, and IPO underwriters may require sunset provisions. The cap-table report shows the resulting voting concentration in the dual-class summary table.

items.title: Coupled solver did not converge within max_iterations
items.founder_question: Runtime event: the round solver reached its iteration cap without settling on a price. The figures are not converged and must not be relied on. This is a convergence problem in the modelling, not a legal question.
